entities.summary:
Benedict of Alignan was a Benedictine abbot and bishop who played a crucial role in the history of Marseille during the 13th century. Born in 1200, Benedict rose to prominence as the abbot of Nôtre Dame de la Grasse in 1224, where he oversaw the construction of the abbey and promoted the arts and architecture. In 1229, he was appointed as the bishop of Marseille, a position he held until his death in 1268. As bishop, Benedict implemented various reforms and attracted numerous pilgrims and scholars to the city. His legacy extended beyond his administrative duties, as he was a patron of the arts and a supporter of the local clergy. The construction of the abbey and the cathedral of Marseille can be attributed to his efforts, and his influence on the city's architecture and culture can still be seen today. In a 13th-century letter, Benedict wrote, "The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing." This quote reflects his devotion to his faith and his role as a spiritual leader in the community.

The causes of Benedict's significance include his involvement in the construction of the abbey and cathedral of Marseille, his promotion of the arts, and his role as a spiritual leader in the community. The effects of his significance can be seen in the enduring legacy of the abbey, the cathedral, and the city's cultural and religious heritage. The relationships between Benedict and other historical figures include his collaboration with the king of France, his correspondence with the Pope, and his participation in the Council of Siena. Places associated with Benedict include the abbey of Nôtre Dame de la Grasse, the cathedral of Marseille, and the city of Alignan.
